newsitem.title: USA: Yahoo! hit 30 mln page views/day in March.
newsitem.headline: Yahoo! hit 30 mln page views/day in March.

text.p: Yahoo! Inc on Wednesday reported a first quarter profit which topped Wall Street estimates and said its traffic surged to an average of more than 30 million page views a day in March.
This was up 50 percent from the 20 million page views a day Yahoo! reported in December, 1996.
Yahoo! reported net income per share of $0.01 and net income of $210,000 in the first quarter, up from net income of $81,000 in the year ago first quarter.
Yahoo! said International Business Machines Corp had chosen the Yahoo! Network to launch a global ad program.
The $0.01 a share profit topped the per share consensus on Wall Street, which was looking for a loss of $0.03 a share, with estimates ranging from a loss of $0.04 a share to breakeven.
"I think it looks strong," said Paul Noglows, analyst at Hambrecht & Quist in San Francisco, noting his break-even forecast was "the most aggressive estimate on the street."

"We think this shows that the fourth quarter wasn't a fluke and that this will be a profitable company going forward," he said of Yahoo!, which went public in spring 1996 amid a binge of new Internet initial public offerings.
Yahoo! posted a profit of $96,000 in the fourth quarter of 1996, but a loss for the year of $2.3 million.
Yahoo! shares closed up 1-3/16 at 34-7/16.
The company said revenues totaled $9.5 million for the first quarter ended March 31, 1997 compared to revenues of $1.7 million for the first quarter of 1996.

Yahoo! said in a statement that the Internet use metering company PC Meter ranked Yahoo! the number one search and navigation site on the Web for the fifth consecutive quarter, with an overall audience reach of 37.8 percent in February.
PC Meter ranked Yahoo! News and Yahoo! Finance number one sources for general news and financial information on the Web.

Tim Koogle, Yahoo!'s president and chief executive officer, said the company was pleased by the five-fold increase in traffic, as measured by each electronic page displayed in response to a user request, compared with a year ago.
But he also said the growing Internet media company will continue to focus on building its businesses and developing a brand that is recognized on a wordwide basis.

"We are focussing on building Yahoo! services and the Yahoo! brand on a global basis and will continue to place a higher priority on such investments rather than on delivering short-term profits," he said.

Yahoo! said IBM, which is one of the top three Internet advertisers, had selected its network to launch a global Internet advertising program due to begin this month and designed to run through the end of 1997.
Yahoo! said it had added several major advertising accounts during the quarter, including Johnson & Johnson, Lufthansa, Novell Inc and United Parcel Service of America Inc.
The company has also expanded its distribution with the Netscape Guide by Yahoo! service it is launching in the second quarter for Netscape Communications Corp.
The company also added new services in the first quarter, including Yahoo! Chat, which enables Internet users worldwide to communicate with each other, and Yahoo! Classifieds.
The Motley Fool personal investing information service was also added to Yahoo! Finance, which includes portfolio management, charting, company profiles, news and stock quotes.

Yahoo! also launched local services in Seattle, Dallas and Austin, bringing to 10 the number of markets in the United States served by localized Yahoo! services in addition to its Get Local, which reaches more than 30,000 cities.
Yahoo! said its Japan service had more than two million page views a day during the month of March.
(sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau +1 415-846-5400)
